The year 1948 was undoubtedly one of the most illustrious in the history of the Bell Labs, the famous American R&D center. That was the year when the invention of the transistor was announced. It was also the year when mathematician and electrical engineer Claude Elwood Shannon (1916-2001) popularized the unit of measurement known as a bit in a seminal paper entitled A Mathematical Theory of Communication. The term – a pun exploiting the fact that a bit is a small piece of something – is a portmanteau of “binary digit”.

 

Although almost everyone knows the gram is a unit of mass, the second is a unit of time and the meter is a unit of length, it is much less easy to grasp what a bit is the benchmark for. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
